Error SSO-401 means that the SAML assertion signature is invalid, which occurs when the Identity Provider (IdP) has rotated its certificates but Tasklane has not yet received the new ones. To fix this, you must re-upload the current IdP certificate in your settings, as automatic updates are not supported. You should inform the customer to update their IdP certificate configuration immediately to restore SSO functionality.

Yes, the error SSO-409 means the user's email is already associated with a different Tasklane workspace where SSO is enforced. You should tell the customer that the user needs to be removed from the other workspace or must use a different email address to sign in.

The ACS URL for the Tasklane SAML app is https://auth.tasklane.example/saml/acs/<workspace-id>, where <workspace-id> must be replaced with the specific ID of the workspace. This configuration step is part of creating the Tasklane application in your Identity Provider (IdP) as per the setup guide.

A 429 response from the Tasklane API means the client has exceeded the workspace's per-minute request limit (e.g., 60 for Free, 300 for Pro, or 1,000 for Enterprise), and the client must wait at least the number of seconds specified in the Retry-After header before retrying. If the client continues to send requests while limited for more than 5 minutes, they will be temporarily blocked for 15 minutes and receive the API_TEMP_BLOCKED error code instead. The limit applies per workspace, so creating additional tokens does not increase the allowed request count.

Rate limits apply per workspace, not per individual API token. This means that creating additional tokens for a workspace will not increase the total number of requests allowed within the rate limit window; the limit is shared across all tokens associated with that specific workspace [S1].

Consequently, users can still sign in and view content but cannot create or edit tasks, upload files, or run automations [S2][S3].
